appease|propitiate.distinction: Appease concedes to avoid conflict, while propitiate makes an offering to regain the favour of something powerful.

appoint|constitute.distinction: Appoint puts a named person into a post, while constitute forms the body itself or makes up its parts.

apposite|pertinent.distinction: Apposite is strikingly apt, the perfect instance, while pertinent merely bears on the question at hand.

apprehension|savvy.distinction: Apprehension is dread of what is coming, or else grasping an idea, while savvy is shrewd practical know-how.

appropriate|usurp.distinction: Appropriate takes something for your own use, while usurp seizes an office or authority belonging to another.

appurtenance|appurtenant.distinction: An appurtenance is the accessory item itself, while appurtenant is the adjective for what attaches to a greater thing.

appurtenant|auxiliary.distinction: Appurtenant belongs to something as a subordinate part, while auxiliary is separate support brought in to help.

apropos|timely.distinction: Apropos means fitting the subject under discussion, while timely means arriving at the right moment, whatever the topic.

arbitrate|mediate.distinction: An arbitrator hears both sides and imposes a decision, while a mediator only helps the two sides reach their own.

arch|patronizing.distinction: Arch is knowing and teasing, with a glint in it, while patronizing talks down and assumes you understand less.

ardent|fervent.distinction: Ardent is passion burning for a person or a cause, while fervent is intensity poured into what someone says or believes.

ardent|fervid.distinction: Ardent passion is warm and admirable, while fervid runs hotter and usually suggests the heat has become excessive.

ardent|torrid.distinction: Ardent describes passionate feeling, while torrid describes scorching heat, whether of a climate or of a love affair.

ardent|zealous.distinction: Ardent is warmth of feeling, while zealous is energy in pursuit, so a zealous campaigner works where an ardent admirer burns.

ardor|fervor.distinction: Ardor is the warmth of personal passion, while fervor is intensity of conviction, and is the word used of crowds.

ardor|zeal.distinction: Ardor is feeling that burns, while zeal is that feeling turned into tireless effort for a cause.

arduous|laborious.distinction: Arduous is hard because it demands strength and will, while laborious is hard because it is long and full of drudgery.

armada|flotilla.distinction: An armada is a great fleet of warships, while a flotilla is a small group of boats, often civilian ones.

arrant|consummate.distinction: Arrant means utter and always precedes something bad, while consummate means complete and usually praises a skill.

arrant|utter.distinction: Arrant is reserved for utter nonsense and utter knaves, while utter itself attaches to anything, good or bad.

arriviste|parvenu.distinction: An arriviste is still pushing to arrive socially, while a parvenu has arrived and is mocked for how new the money is.

arrogate|usurp.distinction: Arrogate claims a right or the credit you have no title to, while usurp seizes the office or the power itself.

ascendancy|hegemony.distinction: Ascendancy is having gained the upper hand, while hegemony is settled dominance one power holds over others.

ascetic|austere.distinction: An ascetic denies himself pleasure on principle, while austere describes anything plain and unadorned, including a room.

ascribe|attribute.distinction: Ascribe assigns a cause or an authorship to something, while an attribute is a quality the thing simply has.

ascribe|impute.distinction: Ascribe assigns an origin neutrally, while impute lays a fault or a motive at someone's door, usually unfavourably.

asperity|rigor.distinction: Asperity is harshness in someone's tone, while rigor is strictness of method, and can be wholly admirable.

aspersion|calumny.distinction: An aspersion is a slur dropped in passing, while calumny is a sustained false charge meant to destroy a reputation.

aspersion|slander.distinction: An aspersion is an insinuation, often indirect, while slander is a false spoken statement the law can punish.

assert|aver.distinction: Assert states something firmly, while aver adds that you positively know it to be true and will stand behind it.

assert|avow.distinction: Assert puts a claim forward, while avow admits openly something others might have expected you to hide.

assiduous|diligent.distinction: Assiduous is unremitting attention that never lets up, while diligent is steady conscientious care.

assiduous|industrious.distinction: Assiduous is persistent close attention to one task, while industrious is hardworking across whatever there is to do.

assimilate|incorporate.distinction: Assimilate absorbs something until it cannot be told apart, while incorporate includes it as an identifiable part.

assuage|conciliate.distinction: Assuage soothes a feeling, while conciliate wins a person back and repairs the relationship itself.

assuage|mollify.distinction: Assuage eases any strong feeling, including grief and hunger, while mollify only softens anger.

assuage|palliate.distinction: Assuage eases the feeling itself, while palliate eases symptoms while the underlying trouble remains.

assuage|slake.distinction: Assuage soothes distress of any kind, while slake satisfies a specific appetite, above all thirst.

attribute|impute.distinction: An attribute is a quality something possesses, while to impute is to assign a motive or a fault to someone.

audacious|brazen.distinction: Audacious is bold enough to admire, while brazen is bold without shame and expects you to disapprove.

audacious|hardy.distinction: Audacious is daring in what it attempts, while hardy is tough in what it endures.

audacious|intrepid.distinction: Audacious takes risks that may be reckless, while intrepid is steady fearlessness in the face of real danger.

audacity|temerity.distinction: Audacity can be admired as nerve, while temerity is always rash boldness someone had no business showing.

austere|spartan.distinction: Austere is plain and severe by choice or taste, while spartan is bare to the point of hardship, with no comfort at all.

austere|stark.distinction: Austere is deliberately unadorned, while stark is bleak and absolute, as in a stark contrast or a stark landscape.

authoritarian|autocratic.distinction: Authoritarian describes a system demanding obedience, while autocratic describes one person ruling with unchecked power.

authoritarian|despotic.distinction: Authoritarian rule enforces strict obedience, while despotic rule adds cruelty and treats the state as personal property.

authoritarian|dictatorial.distinction: Authoritarian describes the regime's character, while dictatorial describes the domineering manner of the person in charge.

autocratic|despotic.distinction: Autocratic means the power is held by one person alone, while despotic adds that the power is used oppressively.

autocratic|dictatorial.distinction: Autocratic is about where power sits, while dictatorial is about how someone behaves, and can describe a committee chair.

autocratic|magisterial.distinction: Autocratic power allows no challenge, while magisterial authority commands respect through mastery rather than force.

autocratic|peremptory.distinction: Autocratic describes how someone rules, while peremptory describes a single order that allows no reply.

avarice|cupidity.distinction: Avarice is the settled vice of hoarding wealth, while cupidity is the eager grasping desire for more of it.

avert|deflect.distinction: Avert stops a disaster from happening at all, while deflect turns something aside so that it lands elsewhere.

aver|avow.distinction: Aver insists that something is true, while avow openly admits something about yourself you might have concealed.

axiom|maxim.distinction: An axiom is a truth assumed so that a proof can proceed, while a maxim is a rule of conduct for how to live.

badger|beleaguer.distinction: Badger is pestering someone with demands, while beleaguer surrounds them with troubles on every side.

badinage|banter.distinction: Badinage is banter with a French polish, light and witty, while banter is the everyday teasing between friends.

baleful|ominous.distinction: Baleful is actively menacing, as in a baleful glare, while ominous merely signals that something bad is coming.

balk|deterrent.distinction: To balk is to stop short and refuse, while a deterrent is the thing that puts someone off before they start.

banality|bromide.distinction: A banality is any obvious dull remark, while a bromide is a soothing platitude offered to settle someone down.

banality|platitude.distinction: A banality is simply dull, while a platitude is dressed up as wisdom and offered as though it meant something.

banal|hackneyed.distinction: Banal is dull because it is obvious, while hackneyed is dull because repetition has worn the life out of it.

banal|stock.distinction: Banal is tediously ordinary, while a stock phrase or character is a ready-made item pulled off the shelf.

banal|threadbare.distinction: Banal was never interesting in the first place, while threadbare once was and has been worn out by use.

banal|trite.distinction: Banal is flat and unoriginal, while trite is specifically worn out by overuse, as a trite phrase is.

banish|ostracize.distinction: Banish drives someone out by authority, while ostracize is a group quietly agreeing to shut a person out.

banter|chaff.distinction: Banter is teasing conversation, while chaff is the husk thrown off from grain, and by extension worthless stuff.

banter|raillery.distinction: Banter is casual give and take, while raillery is more pointed teasing, though still good-natured.

baroque|ornate.distinction: Ornate simply means heavily decorated, while baroque is ornate to the point of extravagance and complexity.

barren|bleak.distinction: Barren means nothing will grow or come of it, while bleak means cold, exposed and offering no comfort or hope.

bawdy|ribald.distinction: Bawdy humour is indecent about sex and enjoys it, while ribald is coarse and irreverent, mocking as much as titillating.

becoming|decorous.distinction: Becoming means it suits the particular person, while decorous means it meets the standard of proper behaviour for anyone.

becoming|seemly.distinction: Becoming flatters the person wearing or doing it, while seemly is what good taste permits in the circumstances.

befuddled|bemused.distinction: Befuddled is muddled and unable to think straight, while bemused is puzzled and a little detached, not drunk.

beguile|enchant.distinction: Beguile charms you, often into being deceived, while enchant simply delights, with no trick behind it.

beguile|hoodwink.distinction: Beguile deceives by charming you into it, while hoodwink is a plain trick with no charm involved at all.

beleaguer|besiege.distinction: Besiege surrounds a place to force surrender, while beleaguer is the harassment that leaves someone beset on all sides.

beleaguer|circumvent.distinction: Beleaguer presses on an obstacle from every side, while circumvent goes cleverly around it instead.

belittle|denigrate.distinction: Belittle makes something sound unimportant, while denigrate blackens a reputation with unfair attack.

belittle|disparage.distinction: Belittle makes something sound small, while disparage runs it down in words to lower everyone else's opinion of it.

belligerent|pugnacious.distinction: A belligerent person or country is already hostile, while a pugnacious one is simply eager to pick a fight.

belligerent|truculent.distinction: Belligerent is aggression already in motion, while truculent is a defiant readiness to fight that shows in the manner.

bemoan|lament.distinction: Bemoan is complaining regret about how things are, while lament is fuller mourning, usually for something or someone lost.

berate|chide.distinction: Berate is angry scolding at length, while chide is a mild reproof that stops well short of anger.

beseech|conjure.distinction: Beseech is begging urgently, while conjure calls something up as if by magic, and only rarely means to entreat solemnly.

beseech|entreat.distinction: Beseech is the more urgent and anguished asking, while entreat is earnest and humble, quieter in tone.

beseech|supplicate.distinction: Beseech is urgent begging of anyone at all, while supplicate carries the posture of kneeling before someone with power.

besiege|circumvent.distinction: Besiege surrounds an obstacle and presses hard on it, while circumvent goes round it and avoids the fight entirely.

besmirch|denigrate.distinction: Besmirch stains a reputation, often by mere association, while denigrate attacks it directly in words.

besmirch|slander.distinction: Besmirch is any staining of a good name, while slander is the specific spoken falsehood, and a legal wrong.

besmirch|sully.distinction: Besmirch and sully both stain a name; besmirch is the public smearing, sully the quieter loss of purity.

bestow|impart.distinction: Bestow hands over a gift or an honour, while impart passes on something less tangible, like knowledge or a flavour.

betoken|foreshadow.distinction: Betoken is a present sign of what is already the case, while foreshadow points forward to an event still to come.

bilious|dyspeptic.distinction: Bilious is bad temper with a sour liverish edge, while dyspeptic is irritable gloom, named from indigestion.

bilk|fleece.distinction: Bilk cheats someone out of what they are owed, while fleece strips a customer bare by overcharging them.

bilk|foil.distinction: Bilk cheats a person out of money, while foil simply stops a plan from succeeding.

bilk|frustrate.distinction: Bilk takes money by cheating, while frustrate blocks an effort without any money changing hands.

bilk|swindle.distinction: Bilk and swindle both cheat someone of money; swindle is the broad confidence trick, bilk often a failure to pay what is due.

bland|insipid.distinction: Bland is simply without flavour or edge, while insipid says the same thing with contempt, of food or of art.
